title: Dashboard inventory figure does not change when a part is set inactive
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-DASHKEEP-01) is tracked at {Location-A} with 4 in its default bin at Cost $12.50 ($50.00 of stock) and is active at the start.
  • The Dashboard's inventory value figure at {Location-A}, read before the steps, is {Total-A} (for example $10,450.00).
custom_steps:
1. On Parts → Inventory, Active tab, search {Part-A}, click its row, pick Part Status "Inactive", click Save, leave the note empty and click "Deactivate" in the "Deactivate part?" confirmation.
  2. Open the Dashboard again and read the inventory value figure.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Part-A} moves to the Inactive tab.
  • Step 2: The figure equals {Total-A} (a difference of $0.00): the $50.00 of {Part-A}'s stock still counts. If someone else changed stock at {Location-A} in the meantime, say so in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S9-E11, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas 13 Oct copy: no board shows the dashboard. Product's 9 Oct answer (Chris Ward, question 13): Dashboard v1 ships first. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-E11: “Reports keep inactive parts. Inventory Value, Parts Velocity and the dashboard include them, because their stock still has value and their history still happened.”
  • PRD §2 Feature Overview, Accounting: “The dashboard's inventory figure and the opening inventory used for accounting keep untracked parts, because that stock still sits in the books.”
